newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-AFRICAN MINNOWS GIVEN RARE MOMENT OF GLORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AFRICAN MINNOWS GIVEN RARE MOMENT OF GLORY.

text.p: Minnows from Africa's smallest, and rarely successful footballing nations, have a rare chance to hog the limelight in the preliminary rounds of African club competition this weekend.

Clubs from exotic countries like the Cape Verde Islands, Equatorial Guinea and the Seychelles are involved in preliminary round, second leg matches in the African Champions Cup, the African Cup Winners' Cup and the Confederation of African Football (CAF) Cup.

Cape Verdian club Desportivo Travadores have the best chance of progressing into the first round of the African Champions Cup, having lost by a single goal to Mogas '90 of Benin in the first leg earlier this month.
The workers' team will be at home in the second leg on Sunday in the Cape Verdian capital of Praia.
Cafe Band Sportif and Akonangui of Equatorial Guinea both have uphill tasks in their respective games in Malabo.
Cafe Band Sportif trail 1-4 to Congolese club Munisport in the Champions Cup while Akonangui are 0-3 down to Renaissance of Chad in the African Cup Winners' Cup.
But Akonangui can take heart from the fact that Renaissance's last away appearance in the Cup Winners' Cup three years ago saw them lose 13-0 -- a record margin in African competition.

A 2-1 home defeat for Saint Michel United of the Seychelles in their Champions Cup preliminary round, first leg game against Madagascan team FC BFV two weeks ago leaves them with little chance in Sunday's return in Antananarivo.
But soccer fans on the tropical island will be buoyed by the unexpected progress of Red Stars FC in the Cup Winners' Cup.

They move straight into the second round of the competition in May after preliminary round opponents Club "S" Namakia of Madagascar and first round opponents Maxaquene of Mozambique withdrew from the competition because of financial constraints.
It is the furthest any team from the island have progressed in African club competition.

Liberian club Junior Professionals are another side who can bring some joy to a beleaguered local soccer-loving population, leading 2-0 from the first leg of their Champions Cup tie against Racing Club Bobo Dialassou of Burkina Faso.
The team, who are financed by George Weah, will be away for Sunday's second leg.
